title: Phlebotomine Sand Flies of the Oriental Region
subtitle: Identification keys, species pages and terminology
journals: Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health
rank_conventions: Idiophlebotomus, Grassomyia and Chinius are treated as genera; subgenera of Phlebotomus and Sergentomyia follow Lewis 1978/1982 unless a newer source in sources.csv says otherwise (log the difference in conflicts.csv).
home_image_alt: Head of a female phlebotomine (Galati et al. 2017, CC BY)
home_intro_html:
Phlebotomine sand flies (Diptera: Psychodidae: Phlebotominae) transmit Leishmania, phleboviruses and Bartonella. Identification rests on microscopic characters of slide-mounted adults: the cibarium and pharynx, spermathecae and antennae of females, and the genitalia of males.

This site brings together the published dichotomous keys for the Oriental Region and updates them with later taxonomic work on Thailand and neighbouring countries.
quick_start_html:
• Clear and slide-mount the specimen. Sex it (female spermathecae / male genitalia).
  • Open Lewis 1978 and use Step through. At each couplet choose the lead that fits.
  • Read any ⚠ note on the leads you passed: later work may have split the species.
  • Open the species page: compare the diagnostic notes, conflicting characters and figures.
  • Unsure of a term? See the glossary.
keys_advice_html: Specimen from Thailand or mainland SE Asia? Start with Lewis 1978 (the most complete key), check the result against Quate 1962, then read the species page, which lists species described after these keys.
glossary_intro_html: Older keys (Lewis, Quate) use older terms. The preferred terms follow Galati et al. 2017, the consensus terminology agreed at ISOPS IX. Thumbnails open the illustrating figure.
